To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) aliphatic and positively charged amino acids are the most common residues of αAMP, and (2) the membrane insertion pattern of the N- and C-terminal regions of αAMP is oblique and less structured, respectively, and the central part is a bend structure.

the membrane partitioning energy profiles of 63--166 α-helical AMPs suggest an oblique helical structure for the N-terminal region, a central bend and a less structured parallel structure for the C-terminal region.
the N-termini of antimicrobial peptides are composed of oblique α-helices and their membrane partitioning energies are calculated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sequence analysis and structural prediction of αAMPs and the structural motif of the membrane disruption of αAMPs.
the structural characteristics of antimicrobial peptides.
the structural features of αAMPs and the membrane partitioning energies, and provides some clues for understanding the structure and mechanism of action of αAMPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the membrane-disruptive mechanism of αAMPs is the formation of oblique α-helices in the lipid bilayer, which results in membrane disruption.

the membrane disruptive mechanism of αAMPs is a two-step process: (1) the N-terminal oblique α- helix of αAMPs inserts into the membrane and (2) the C-terminus of the peptide inserts into and/or interacts with the membrane surface.
the first 13 residues of αAMP are the most critical for its antimicrobial function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the membrane partitioning energy of a peptide is a good measure for the membrane disruptive potential of the peptide.
the membrane partitioning energy profile of αAMPs is consistent with the experimentally derived membrane structure of the influenza virus fusion peptide.
the membrane-disruptive activity is determined by the N-terminal oblique helical structure of αAMPs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N-terminal oblique α helix is an important feature of the membrane-disruptive peptide, and the central bend is also important in the membrane insertion of αAMP.
the N-terminal 13 residues of αAMP are responsible for membrane interaction, and that a central bend structure at positions from 13 to 14 may be important for membrane disruption.
the N-terminal 13 residues are important for the biological function of αAMPs, and the C-terminus may play an auxiliary role in the function of αAMP.
